root_idea.summary: The root centers on weighty solidity: thickness, density, compactness, and heaviness.
root_idea.development: The physical idea of being thick or compact develops into causing heaviness or incapacitation, especially through wounding, and into figurative applications involving gravity, exertion, effect, and being overcome.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form IV verb is presented under the normalized perfect citation form أَثْخَنَ.

senses.definition: To inflict severe slaughter or wounding on an enemy, thereby weakening or overcoming them.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic battle constructions أَثْخَنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ and أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ, the action involves making the enemy heavy or incapacitated through extensive slaughter or wounding. Contextual renderings include fighting strenuously and subduing them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thick, dense, compact, coarse, hard, firm, stiff, tough, or strong; of a semiliquid, to become so thick that it does not flow freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of things and materials, including cloth and semiliquids.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something thick or dense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary physical causative use of Form IV.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone heavy, weak, languid, or enervated, especially by beating or wounding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person; wounds or disease may be the means or cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the usual or proper bounds in an affair; to strive vigorously or do one's utmost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي in the construction أَثْخَنَ فِي الأَمْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a saying to affect, distress, or afflict someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction in which the saying is the agent of the effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To know or be acquainted with someone thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَثْخَنَ فُلَانًا مَعْرِفَةً.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavy, weakened, languid, or enervated through wounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a poetic war expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome by sleep, or to become overcome by disease and fatigue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as اِسْتَثْخَنَ مِنْهُ النَّوْمُ and اِسْتَثْخَنَ بَيْنَ الْمَرَضِ وَالإِعْيَاءِ.
Used substantively, especially of a garment or piece of cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported heaviness in the chest or body, or heaviness and languor affecting the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tentative lexical report whose transmitted reading may be confused with related forms for thickness or heaviness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, dense, coarse, big, firm, tough, or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of cloth, it may describe a close or full texture, including the warp.
Applied to a man described as ثَخِينُ السِّلَاحِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Forbearing, clement, grave, sedate, or calm; figuratively, weighty in bearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, including one characterized as heavy in his sitting-place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakened, languid, enervated, or heavily wounded; beaten until nearly at the point of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participle of Form IV, describing a person left in a severely weakened condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Forbearing, clement, grave, sedate, or calm in mind or intellect.
A person who causes laughter, or who is quick, brisk, or lively in movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymical usage reported in the speech of Syria.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who exceeds the usual or proper bounds or does his utmost in narration and the rehearsal of sayings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person characterized by excessive or extreme narration.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The general Form IV battle construction is covered by the same severe-slaughter and wounding branch attested in Quranic usage.
Pointer-only cross-reference; it adds no independent lexical definition.

cautions: Lane's historical Quran citation notation is not converted into modern verse coordinates; the Quran examples use the independently supplied QAC locations 8:67 and 47:4.
The reported ثَخَنٌ sense is textually tentative and is retained as such rather than treated as an unqualified core meaning.
